result.title: Rethinking Least-Core Computation in Contextual-Distractor Games
result.summary: Game-theoretic attribution explains a model by assigning credit to its features or training examples. The least core has attracted interest as an alternative to Shapley-style averaging because it can expose players that cause substantial harm in rare, high-value contexts. However, least-core allocations are generally nonunique, and the choice of allocation can affect the resulting explanation. In this study, we investigate how payoff selection and coalition sampling affect least-core attribution. Our experiments show that selector choice matters for distinguishing useful and harmful contributions, and that sampling can degrade harmful-player identification across the tested selectors even when useful players remain well identified. These observations motivate efficient computation with all coalition constraints and a well-defined selector. We introduce entropic least core (ELC), a smooth approximation whose unique minimizer follows a continuous path along the temperature to the nucleolus, a classical refinement of the least core. Our experiments show that ELC approximates the nucleolus faster than an LP-based nucleolus solver while retaining small payoff errors, with further GPU acceleration at larger problem sizes. In the tested full-coalition contextual-distractor games, ELC matches the minimum-norm selector in identification accuracy and more accurately ranks distractors by harm.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究博弈论归因中的 least core 计算：分析收益选择器与联盟采样对解释结果的影响，并提出「entropic least core」（ELC），用沿温度连续路径逼近 nucleolus 的光滑近似来实现唯一且高效的计算。实验显示 ELC 比基于 LP 的 nucleolus 求解器更快，且在识别有害干扰项上更准确。
AI.relevance_reason: least core 用于在稀有高价值语境下找出造成实质损害的「玩家」，与 LVR 中视觉干扰项筛选、视觉证据/贡献分配的评价问题可能相关：其收益选择器与联盟采样偏差的分析可供核查 latent 内容归因的因果分配与监督设计。
